findings.location: Definition 3.2 p.10; Proposition 3.3 p.11; Lemma 3.7 p.12; Lemma 8.3 p.20
findings.claim: Every ergodic Gibbs u-state is either a center isometry or has a contracting full-cu-volume set contained in supp(mu).
findings.hypotheses: Compact complex threefold; genuine product center fibration; stable multiplier (3-sqrt(5))/2<1/2 and unstable multiplier (3+sqrt(5))/2>2; spherical center derivative between 1/2 and 2; Haar base mixing and Gibbs u condition verified.
findings.decisive_evidence: supp(mu)=T4 x {0} intersects each four-real-dimensional cu plaque in a two-dimensional unstable plaque, of volume zero. Any bounded invariant fiber metric would satisfy a(A^n b)=2^n a(b) at the attracting fixed point, impossible. Neither alternative holds.
findings.impact: The central dichotomy and its invocation in Lemma 8.3 fail as stated. No counterexample to Theorem 1.3: the product has holomorphic center.
findings.repair: Remove B subset supp(mu), or allow B in the center saturation of supp(mu). Lemma 3.7 constructs such a larger set; Section 4 uses its full-volume property, not the invalid support restriction.
findings.limits: Verified counterexample and compatible repair; author adoption and journal correction not verified.

findings.location: Example 10.2 p.25, explicitly Proof of Theorem 1.5
findings.claim: The displayed F is an automorphism of the Lie algebra with [e1,e2]=[e3,e4]=e5.
findings.decisive_evidence: [F e1,F e2]=5e5 versus F[e1,e2]=e5; [F e1,F e4]=3e5 versus zero. All basis pairs independently computed; four nonzero residuals. FJ=JF holds but cannot imply a group lift.
findings.impact: The stated lift is impossible and the supplied construction does not prove Theorem 1.5.
findings.repair: A different type-(1,1) bracket with Q=[[-2,1],[1,2]], A^TQA=Q, determinant -5 yields an integrable J and valid F. Retain a BCH-closed half-central lattice and consistent left-quotient convention; stable/unstable brackets generate one real central dimension, giving five-dimensional accessibility.
findings.limits: Replacement changes construction and checks its feasibility, not original correctness; does not refute theorem or claim author adoption.

findings.location: Example 10.1 p.24; also relevant to lattice assertion within Example 10.2 p.25
findings.claim: The exponential of the integer span of the stipulated Heisenberg basis is a lattice subgroup.
findings.decisive_evidence: BCH gives log(exp e1 exp e2)=e1+e2+(1/2)e3 in Example 10.1, outside the integer span.
findings.impact: The indicated illustrative quotient is undefined; with a genuine lattice the same map and algebra give the accessible example. Principal rigidity and higher-dimensional theorem arguments do not depend on this integer-span specification.
findings.repair: Use half Gaussian integers in the complex central coordinate, integral horizontal coordinates; BCH and the integral determinant-one automorphism preserve this subgroup in both directions.
findings.limits: Theorem 1.5 additionally requires the independent bracket repair in P2; lattice correction alone does not repair P2.

findings.claim: W=L^(direct sum 2n), but degree(det W)=n degree(L).
findings.decisive_evidence: det W=L^(tensor 2n), hence degree(det W)=2n degree(L); n=2 yields 4d, not 2d.
findings.impact: Only positivity is used and is preserved, so nontriviality/non-Kahler argument is unaffected.

checks.derivation: The product f(b,z)=(Ab,z/2) on E^2 x P1 is a compact fibered holomorphic threefold. The base multipliers (3?sqrt5)/2 strictly dominate spherical center derivative 2(1+r^2)/(4+r^2), bounded between 1/2 and 2. Haar x delta0 is an ergodic Gibbs-u state, with support of real dimension 4 and intersection of real dimension 2 in each 4-dimensional cu plaque. Thus every allowed subset of support has cu volume zero. Any bounded invariant fiber metric gives a(A^n b)=2^n a(b) at the attracting fixed point, impossible on an invariant full-measure set.
